text: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the core document is titled 'FAILURE MECHANISM BASED STRESS TEST QUALIFICATION FOR INTEGRATED CIRCUITS', establishing the foundational framework for qualifying automotive-grade integrated circuits through targeted stress testing.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Table of Contents lists the main body and seven appendices, including Appendix 1 on the Definition of a Qualification Family and Appendix 7 on the use of Mission Profiles, providing a structured overview of the document's scope.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the document includes a series of attachments designated AEC-Q100-001 through AEC-Q100-012, which are specific test method standards, such as AEC-Q100-001 for Wire Bond Shear Test and AEC-Q100-011 for Charged Device Model (CDM) ESD Test.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Revision Summary outlines key changes from the prior Rev-G version, noting that punctuation and text improvements are not detailed, focusing instead on substantive technical and procedural updates.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Section 1.2.1 was updated to add a reference to the AEC-Q005 Pb-Free Requirements document, expanding the list of automotive reference documents considered for qualification.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a new Section 1.2.4 was created to address Decommissioned Reference Documents, specifically guiding the removal of AEC-Q100-003 (Machine Model ESD) due to industry obsolescence and AEC-Q100-006 (Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage) due to lack of industry need.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Section 1.3.1 on AEC Q100 Qualification was amended to recommend that the passing ESD voltage level be specified in the supplier datasheet, including footnotes for any pin exceptions.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a new Section 1.3.2 titled 'AEC Certification' was added to clarify that formal 'certification' by the AEC does not exist; instead, suppliers perform qualification testing according to AEC standards.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Section 1.3.4 on the Definition of Part Operating Temperature Grade was revised to include a new Table 1 defining grades and providing guidance on temperature measurement points, while eliminating the Grade 4 entry.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a new Section 1.3.5 was introduced to define 'Capability Measure, Cpk' and provide a reference to the AEC-Q003 Characterization document for further details.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Section 2.2 on the Precedence of Requirements was updated with clarifications to the entries for Purchase Order and Device Specification, detailing the hierarchy of governing documents.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Section 2.3.1 on the Definition of Generic Data was modified, with its existing Table 1 (Part Qualification/Requalification Lot Requirements) and a portion of its text moved to the newly defined Appendix 1.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Section 2.3.2 was updated to add content regarding the Time Limit for Acceptance of Generic Data, establishing validity periods for previously generated qualification data.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the appendices serve specialized purposes; for example, Appendix 5 details Part Design Criteria to Determine Need for EMC Testing, and Appendix 6 covers criteria for SER (Soft Error Rate) Testing.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the attachments include both active and decommissioned test methods, such as AEC-Q100-005 for Nonvolatile Memory Write/Erase Endurance and Data Retention testing, and the decommissioned AEC-Q100-003 for Machine Model ESD.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, suppliers must conduct qualification testing in accordance with AEC standards, which serves as the foundational requirement for all subsequent technical specifications and revisions.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1.3.4 introduces a new Table 1 that defines part operating temperature grades and provides guidance on using specific temperature points (e.g., endpoint, junction) during testing, while also eliminating the Grade 4 entry from the standard.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, a new Section 1.3.5 is added to define the Capability Measure (Cpk) and includes a reference to the AEC-Q003 Characterization document for further details on process capability assessment.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 2.2 on the Precedence of Requirements has been updated with clarifying text regarding the hierarchy between Purchase Orders and Device Specifications.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 2.3.1 has been revised, moving the existing Table 1 on Part Qualification/Requalification Lot Requirements and a portion of the section text to a new Appendix 1, which defines a Product Qualification Family.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 2.3.2 now includes additional explanatory text regarding the use of the diagram presented in Figure 1 for understanding the time limits for accepting generic data.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 2.4.1 on Lot Requirements has been amended to state that any deviation from the requirements outlined in Table 2 must be accompanied by a technical explanation.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 2.5, which defines a Test Failure After Stressing, has been updated with a new statement concerning Electrical Overstress (EOS) conditions.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the entire Section 3.1.1 on 'Qualification of A New Device Manufactured in A Currently Qualified Family' has been deleted, as its subject matter is now comprehensively covered in Appendix 1.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 3.2.3 on 'Criteria for Passing Requalification' has been modified to provide clearer and more actionable guidance for the AEC-Q100 requalification process.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, a new Section 3.3 has been added, detailing specific qualification requirements for Pb-Free devices and referencing the AEC-Q005 Pb-Free Requirements document for compliance.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Figure 2 (Qualification Test Flow) has been updated: Test Group A removes the 'PC before PTC' statement; Test Group B corrects the post-HTOL test temperature order to Room, Cold, & Hot; and Test Group E eliminates references to MM ESD and GL tests.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Table 2 (Qualification Test Methods) shows significant revisions: Test A4 (Temperature Cycling) has its low-end temperature and minimum duration revised, includes a legacy temperature note, and removes the Grade 4 entry; Tests A6 and A7 (High Temperature Storage Life and Operating Life) add references to ambient (Ta) and junction (Tj) temperatures, with A7 also removing the 408-hour duration option.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Table 2 continues with key modifications: Tests C1, C2, C4, C5 (Wire Bond Shear, Wire Bond Pull, Physical Dimension, Solder Ball Shear) all remove the Ppk requirement, change the accept criterion to Cpk > 1.67, and add a reference to AEC-Q003; Test C3 (Solderability) adds a reference to J-STD-002D and a statement on dry bake use.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the final entries in Table 2 include: the elimination of Test E8 (Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage); the addition of a new Test E12 for Lead (Pb) Free qualification; updates to Tests F1 and F2 (Part Average Testing and Statistical Bin/Yield Analysis) with modified guidance on sample sizes and accept criteria; and a modification to Test G1 (Mechanical Shock) regarding sample size per lot and the number of lots required.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) Human Body Model (HBM) section has been updated by eliminating the Machine Model (MM) ESD test entry and adding a reference to Section 1.3.1 for further details.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test E3 for Electrostatic Discharge Charged Device Model has been revised to include a new reference directing users to Section 1.3.1 for relevant information.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test E5 for Electrical Distribution now includes an explicit acceptance criterion of Cpk>1.67 and adds a reference to the AEC-Q003 standard.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test E8 for Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage has been completely eliminated from the qualification requirements.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a new Test E12 for Lead (Pb) Free compliance has been added as a mandatory entry in the test catalog.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test F1 for Part Average Testing has been modified, with its Additional Requirements section now providing specific guidance on statistical sample sizes and acceptance criteria.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test F2 for Statistical Bin/Yield Analysis has been updated, with its Additional Requirements revised to offer guidance on determining appropriate sample sizes and acceptance criteria.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, multiple mechanical tests (G1 Mechanical Shock, G2 Variable Frequency Vibration, G3 Constant Acceleration, and G4 Gross/Fine Leak) have been revised, each modifying the required sample size per lot and the number of lots for qualification.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test G8 for Internal Water Vapor has been updated, specifically modifying the required sample size per lot for the test.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Table 2's Legend has been amended to include a reference to Note L, which pertains specifically to Lead-Free (Pb-Free) devices.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Table 3 - Process Change Qualification Guidelines for the Selection of Tests has been revised by removing the MM (Machine Model) ESD and GL (Gate Leakage) entries and adding a new LF (Lead Free) test entry.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Appendix 1 – Definition of a Product Qualification Family has undergone a complete revision, and includes new sections A1.1 (Product) and A1.4 (Qualification/Requalification Lot Requirements), with Table 1 from Rev G relocated and renumbered as Table A1.1.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the revised Table A1.1 – Part Qualification/Requalification Lot Requirements has deleted the row for 'A new part that has some applicable generic data' and added a new entry for scenarios where 'The part to be qualified is slightly more complex', accompanied by a new Table A1.2 providing examples for generic data use.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Appendix Template 4A (Qualification Test Plan) and 4B (Generic Data) show synchronized updates: Test C3 (Solderability) now references J-STD-002D and requires steam aging; Test E2 eliminates the MM entry; Test E8 eliminates the GL entry; and Tests G1-G4 (Hermetic Package Tests) have modified sample size and lot requirements, with Appendix 4B's Generic Data Part Attributes Section also completely revised.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a new Appendix 7 – Guideline on Relationship of Robustness Validation to AEC-Q100 has been added, containing explanatory text, new Figures A7.1 & A7.2, and a new Table A7.1 to illustrate the relationship.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the file acknowledges the collaborative effort behind its creation, recognizing significant contributors from Sustaining Members, Technical Members, Associate Members, Guest Members, and Other Contributors within the Automotive Electronics Council.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the NOTICE section clarifies that AEC documents are prepared and approved by the AEC Technical Committee, serving the automotive electronics industry by eliminating misunderstandings and facilitating product interchangeability and improvement.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the NOTICE explicitly states that adoption of AEC documents does not consider potential patent involvement, and AEC assumes no liability to patent owners or obligations to adopting parties, with conformance claims requiring all document requirements to be met.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the NOTICE specifies that inquiries about the document should be directed to the AEC Technical Committee via http://www.aecouncil.com, and the document is published by the Automotive Electronics Council with copyright retained by AEC.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the copyright notice indicates the document may be downloaded free of charge but not resold, is printed in the U.S.A., and can be freely reprinted with the copyright notice but cannot be changed without AEC Component Technical Committee approval.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the title 'FAILURE MECHANISM BASED STRESS TEST QUALIFICATION FOR PACKAGED INTEGRATED CIRCUITS' establishes the document's core subject: defining qualification requirements based on stress tests that target failure mechanisms in packaged ICs.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, it is noted that text enhancements and differences since the last revision are shown as underlined areas, with several revised figures and tables whose changes are not underlined, and the standard's implementation date for new qualifications is the publish date unless stated otherwise.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1 SCOPE defines the document as containing a set of failure mechanism based stress tests that set minimum qualification requirements for integrated circuits (ICs), aiming to accelerate failures compared to use conditions.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the SCOPE section cautions that these accelerated tests should not be used indiscriminately; each qualification project must be examined for potential new failure mechanisms, tests inducing non-application failures, or extreme use conditions reducing acceleration.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the SCOPE clarifies that using this document does not relieve the IC supplier of their internal qualification program responsibilities, defines 'user' as all customers using a device qualified per this spec, and encourages suppliers to use stated device temperature grades in part information.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1.1 PURPOSE states the specification's aim is to determine if a device can pass specified stress tests, thereby providing an expected level of quality/reliability in the application.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1.2 REFERENCE DOCUMENTS specifies that the current revision of referenced documents is effective at the qualification plan agreement date, with subsequent plans automatically using updated revisions of these documents.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1.2.1 lists Automotive reference documents: AEC-Q001 Guidelines for Part Average Testing, AEC-Q002 Guidelines for Statistical Yield Analysis, AEC-Q003 Guidelines for Characterizing Electrical Performance, AEC-Q004 Zero Defects Guideline (DRAFT), AEC-Q005 Pb-Free Requirements, and SAE J1752/3 Integrated Circuits Radiated Emissions Measurement Procedure.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1.2.2 begins listing Military reference documents, though the provided text cuts off, indicating the document structure includes a section for military standards alongside automotive ones.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the header mentions the inclusion of NEW Figures A7.1 & A7.2 and NEW Table A7.1, highlighting specific updated visual aids within the document's appendices or technical sections.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the primary purpose of the specification is defined as establishing a method to determine a device's capability to pass specified stress tests, thereby providing an expected level of quality and reliability in its application.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the section on reference documents specifies that the current revisions of all referenced documents are effective at the date of agreement to the qualification plan, with subsequent plans automatically adopting updated revisions of these documents.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, key automotive reference documents are listed, including AEC-Q001 for Part Average Testing, AEC-Q002 for Statistical Yield Analysis, AEC-Q003 for Characterizing Electrical Performance, AEC-Q004 (DRAFT) for Zero Defects, AEC-Q005 for Pb-Free Requirements, and SAE J1752/3 for Integrated Circuits Radiated Emissions Measurement Procedure.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the military reference document specified is MIL-STD-883, which outlines Test Methods and Procedures for Microelectronics.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, several industrial reference documents are enumerated, such as JEDEC JESD-22 for Reliability Test Methods, UL-STD-94 for Flammability Tests, IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 for Moisture/Reflow Sensitivity Classification, and the JESD89 series for measuring Alpha Particle and Cosmic Ray-Induced Soft Errors.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, decommissioned documents are noted, including AEC Q100-003 for ESD Machine Model, removed due to obsolescence as HBM and CDM cover known ESD failures, and AEC Q100-006 for Electrothermally-Induced Gate Leakage, removed due to lack of need as a qualification test.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, AEC Q100 Qualification is defined as the successful completion and documentation of test results per this document's requirements, allowing a supplier to claim a part is 'AEC Q100 qualified', with a recommendation to specify the passing ESD voltage in the datasheet.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, it is clarified that there are no official 'certifications' for AEC-Q100 qualification, nor a certification board; instead, each supplier performs qualification to AEC standards, considers customer requirements, and submits data to the customer for compliance verification.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, 'Approval for Use in an Application' is defined as user approval for using a part in their specific application, with the user's method of approval explicitly stated as beyond the scope of this document.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Definition of Part Operating Temperature Grade is provided, specifying that endpoint test temperatures for hot and cold tests must match the particular grade's specifications, and junction temperature during certain stress tests should meet or exceed the grade's hot temperature.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the capability measure Cpk is mentioned, with a directive to refer to AEC-Q003 Characterization to understand how this statistical measure will be utilized within the standard.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the general objective of the specification is stated as establishing a standard that defines operating temperature grades for integrated circuits based on a minimum set of qualification requirements.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the concept of 'Zero Defects' is introduced within the context of qualification, noting that qualification and other aspects of the document represent a subset of a broader quality framework aimed at minimizing defects.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the logical connection between stress test passage and reliability expectation is established, implying that the specification's purpose is to correlate successful testing with predictable field performance and quality levels.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the hierarchical structure of requirements is implied, beginning with the overarching purpose, moving through referenced standards and definitions, and culminating in general requirements that set the foundation for specific qualification procedures.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, if junction heating is accounted for during powered tests, the hot test endpoint test temperature is permitted to be greater than the standard specified temperature.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, for Test Group B, which includes Accelerated Lifetime Simulation Tests like HTOL, ELFR, and EDR, the device's junction temperature during stressing must meet or exceed the hot temperature designated for its specific operating temperature grade.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Cpk measure, a statistical process control index, is referenced, and its application within the standard is defined by the guidelines provided in the AEC-Q003 Characterization document.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the primary objective of the specification is established as defining integrated circuit operating temperature grades through a foundational set of qualification requirements.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the concept of Zero Defects is introduced, where qualification activities contribute to this goal, with detailed implementation elements found in the AEC-Q004 Zero Defects Guideline.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a strict order of precedence for requirements is defined to resolve conflicts, prioritizing the purchase order, then the individual device specification, this document itself, its referenced documents, and finally the supplier's data sheet.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, it is stipulated that for a device to be qualified per this specification, purchase orders or device specifications cannot waive or reduce the requirements set forth within this base document.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the use of generic data to streamline qualification and requalification is strongly encouraged, allowing early submission to users for assessing additional testing needs.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, generic data must be based on a matrix linking device characteristics and manufacturing processes, as detailed in Table 3 and Appendix 1, and data containing failures is unusable unless corrective action is documented and accepted.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Appendix 1 defines the criteria for grouping components into a qualification family, allowing data from all family members to be considered generically acceptable for qualifying a specific device.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Table 3 outlines a superset of qualification tests required for evaluating new processes or process changes, serving as a baseline for supplier-user discussions, with the supplier responsible for justifying any test omissions.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, there is no time limit for the acceptability of generic data, provided it originates from the specific part or a part within the same qualification family as defined in Appendix 1.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, potential sources for acceptable generic reliability data include anonymized customer-specific data, process change qualification data, and periodic reliability monitor data, as illustrated in Figure 1.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, it is noted that certain process changes, such as a die shrink, can invalidate pre-change data for use as generic data, affecting its acceptability.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, test sample requirements specify that samples must be representative of the qualification family, and when multiple lots are needed, samples must come from non-consecutive wafer and molding lots, separated by at least one non-qualification lot, with deviations requiring technical justification.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, acceptable sources of data for qualification include customer-specific data (with names withheld), process change qualification data, and periodic reliability monitor data, as referenced in Figure 1: Generic Data Time Line.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a critical note specifies that certain process changes, such as a die shrink, can invalidate generic data collected prior to the change, rendering it unacceptable for use in qualification processes.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the requirements for test samples stipulate they must be a representative device from the qualification family, and when multiple lots are needed due to insufficient generic data, samples must be drawn from non-consecutive wafer and molding lots.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, it is mandated that all qualification devices must be manufactured using the exact tooling and processes at the production site that will be utilized for volume part deliveries, though validated alternate electrical test sites may be used for measurements.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the reusability policy states that devices used in nondestructive qualification tests can be reused for other tests, while those used in destructive tests cannot be used further except for engineering analysis purposes.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, sample size requirements dictate that the number of samples used for qualification testing or generic data submission must align with the minimum sample sizes and acceptance criteria specified in Table 2.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the protocol for using generic data requires that specific test conditions and results be recorded and made available to the user, preferably in the format of Appendix 4, with existing applicable data used first before device-specific testing.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, pre- and post-stress test requirements specify that end-point test temperatures, which may include room, hot, and/or cold temperatures, are detailed in the 'Additional Requirements' column of Table 2 for each test.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a test failure after stressing is defined as a device failing to meet the individual device specification, test-specific criteria, or the supplier's data sheet, prioritized as per Section 2.2, with external physical damage from testing also constituting a failure.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, failures caused by mishandling like EOS or ESD, or other non-reliability-related causes, must be discounted from reliability assessments but still reported as part of the data submission.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the qualification process for a new device, outlined in Figure 2 and Table 2, requires the supplier to have data for all stress tests, either from device-specific testing or acceptable generic data, and to review other devices in the same family for common failure mechanisms.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the supplier must provide a Certificate of Design, Construction and Qualification (Appendix 2), Stress Test Qualification data (Table 2 & Appendix 4), and data on the fault grading level of qualification software per Q100-007 for each new device qualification.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, requalification of a changed device is required when a supplier makes any product or process change that impacts or could potentially impact the device's form, fit, function, quality, or reliability, as guided by Table 3.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the supplier is obligated to meet user requirements for product or process change notifications as part of the requalification framework.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, it is established that, at a minimum, any change that affects the product's form, fit, function, quality, or reliability necessitates a full requalification process to ensure continued compliance and reliability.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, initial device qualification necessitates the supplier to possess a Certificate of Design, Construction and Qualification, as detailed in Appendix 2.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, for initial qualification, the supplier must provide Stress Test Qualification data, with references to Table 2 and Appendix 4 for specific requirements.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, qualification also requires data on the fault grading level of the software used, per Q100-007, to be made available to the customer upon request, applicable to relevant device types.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, requalification of a changed device is mandated when a supplier's change impacts or could potentially impact the device's form, fit, function, quality, and/or reliability, as guided by Table 3.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the supplier is required to meet user requirements for product or process changes, as outlined in the Process Change Notification section 3.2.1.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, any change to the product, per Appendix 1, requires performing applicable tests from Table 2, using Table 3 to formulate the requalification test plan and assess the need for generic data.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, passing requalification requires analyzing all failures for root cause and implementing corrective and preventative actions before the part can be considered AEC Q100 qualified again.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, user approval is required for process changes that may affect device performance in a specific application, even if the operating temperature grade is unchanged, though this authorization method is outside the document's scope.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, qualification of a Pb-Free device must address special quality and reliability issues as specified in AEC-Q005, covering materials like termination plating and board attach solder.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Pb-Free processing typically requires higher board attach temperatures for solder joint quality, which may adversely affect moisture sensitivity, potentially necessitating more robust mold compounds.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, if an encapsulation material change is needed for Pb-Free processing robustness, the supplier should refer to the process change qualification requirements within the specification.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, preconditioning for Pb-Free devices must be performed at the Pb-free reflow classification temperatures described in IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 before environmental stress tests.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, general qualification tests are outlined in Figure 2 and Table 2, with applicability depending on device type (e.g., ceramic packages, NVM devices) as noted, and user-requested unique tests require negotiation.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, device-specific tests mandatory for all hermetic and plastic packages include Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) and Latch-up (LU) for all products, disallowing generic data.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Electrical Distribution test requires demonstrating parametric limits over operating conditions using data from at least three lots or one matrixed lot, with a strong recommendation to use AEC-Q001 Guidelines for Part Average Testing to establish final test limits.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, it is mandated that all hermetic and plastic packaged devices must undergo specific device testing for qualification, explicitly prohibiting the use of generic data for these tests, though pre-existing device-specific data is acceptable.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) testing is required for all products as a core qualification test, underscoring its universal applicability across device types.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Latch-up (LU) testing is stipulated as a mandatory requirement for all products, forming an essential part of the device qualification process.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Electrical Distribution test requires the supplier to demonstrate that the device meets parametric limits across operating temperature, voltage, and frequency, with data sourced from at least three lots or one matrixed process lot to ensure statistical validity as per Q100-009.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, it is strongly recommended that final test limits for Electrical Distribution be established using the AEC-Q001 Guidelines For Part Average Testing to enhance reliability assessment.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a provision allows users to require other tests in lieu of generic data based on their specific experience with a particular supplier, adding flexibility to the qualification framework.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Wearout Reliability Tests must be available to the user when qualifying a new technology or material relevant to failure mechanisms, though the full demonstration is not required for every new device qualification.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, specified wearout failure mechanisms include Electromigration, Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (or Gate Oxide Integrity Test) for all MOS technologies, and Hot Carrier Injection for all MOS technologies below 1 micron.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, additional wearout reliability tests listed are Negative Bias Temperature Instability and Stress Migration, covering key semiconductor device degradation modes.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the legend for Table 2 defines critical codes: 'H' for hermetic packages only, 'P' for plastic packages only, 'B' for BGA devices only, 'N' for nondestructive tests, and 'D' for destructive tests where devices cannot be reused.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, further Table 2 legend codes include 'S' for surface mount plastic packages only, 'G' for allowing generic data per Section 2.3 and Appendix 1, and 'K' for using method AEC-Q100-005 to precondition Non-Volatile Memory circuits.
